cards.name: Sony WF-1000XM6
cards.buy_if: you want the best all-round sound, noise cancelling and call quality on any phone.
cards.skip_if: you're all-in on iPhone (AirPods Pro 3), or you want the absolute quietest (Bose).
cards.owners: Owners praise the sound and the battery. The complaint is fit for small ears, and the price.

cards.name: Apple AirPods Pro 3
cards.chip: Best on iPhone · heart rate · hearing aid
cards.buy_if: you use an iPhone — instant pairing, Find My, hearing-aid mode and the best fit Apple has made.
cards.skip_if: you're on Android: half the features vanish.
cards.owners: Owners love the fit and the noise cancelling. Complaints: the case scratches, and batteries can't be replaced.

photo.credit: Photo: Burkhard Mücke, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen)
cards.price: List $299 · $249 in Bose's own September promotion
cards.buy_if: silence on a plane or a train is the whole point.
cards.skip_if: you want long battery life or the best call quality.
cards.owners: Owners say nothing else is this quiet. Complaints: the 6-hour battery and bulky buds.

cards.name: Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro
cards.chip: Galaxy AI · live translate · very comfortable
cards.skip_if: you don't — several features only work with a Galaxy.
cards.owners: Owners praise comfort and sound. Complaints: the touch controls on the stems, and 6 hours with ANC.

photo.credit: Photo: Dinkun Chen, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons (cropped)

cards.name: Google Pixel Buds Pro 2
cards.buy_if: you're on a Pixel or any Android phone and want Gemini in your ear.
cards.owners: Owners love the fit and the battery. Complaint: the ANC is a step behind Sony and Bose.

cards.name: Apple AirPods 5
cards.chip: No ear tips · real ANC · $129 list
cards.buy_if: you hate things in your ear canal but still want some noise cancelling.
cards.skip_if: you want a tight seal for the gym or a plane.
cards.owners: Brand new — early buyers cite the price and ANC on an open fit. Wait for the first reviews if unsure.

photo.credit: Photo: Cheeseburgahhh, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Anker Soundcore Liberty 4 NC
cards.price: List $99.99 · often about $20 off on sale
cards.buy_if: you want 80% of the flagship experience for a quarter of the price.
cards.skip_if: you take a lot of calls — the mics are the weak spot.
cards.owners: Owners call it the best value in earbuds. Complaints: call quality and a big case.

cards.name: EarFun Air Pro 4+
cards.buy_if: battery life matters more to you than the brand on the case.
cards.skip_if: you want a premium build and feel.
cards.owners: Owners praise the battery and the feature list. Complaint: the ANC is only 'good'.

cards.name: Nothing Ear (3)
cards.price: List $179 · often about $30 off on sale
cards.buy_if: you want earbuds that look like nothing else and sound good.
cards.owners: Owners love the look. Complaints: the app, and ANC in wind.

cards.name: Technics EAH-AZ100
cards.buy_if: music quality is the reason you're buying.
cards.skip_if: you take a lot of calls.
cards.owners: Owners rave about the sound. Complaints: call quality and the price.

cards.name: Beats Powerbeats Pro 2
cards.buy_if: your earbuds have to survive a run, a lift and a lot of sweat.
cards.skip_if: you want a small case in your pocket.
cards.owners: Owners praise the never-move fit and the heart-rate sensor. Complaint: the huge case.

photo.credit: Photo: Kyu3a, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons

cards.name: Shokz OpenFit 2+
cards.price: List $199.95 (OpenFit 2: list $179.95, often under $150 on sale)
cards.buy_if: you run or cycle where you must hear cars.
cards.skip_if: you want any noise isolation at all.
cards.owners: Owners love the awareness and comfort. Complaint: sound leaks, and no ANC by design.

photo.credit: Photo: TaurusEmerald, CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons (OpenFit 2 shown, same design)
